findings.title: Debug logging at Error level on every batch, including full ID lists
Cleanup job interval changed from 10 to 1 minute
SQLite parameter-limit workaround is keyed on the configured batch size instead of the ID count, and is fragile
MaxCount cleanup can loop forever or run wastefully when deletes affect 0 rows
Test helper uses require inside the DB session callback and discards the callback's error

response:
## 1) Severity: HIGH | Type: Implementation
Title: Debug logging at Error level on every batch, including full ID lists

Affected:
- pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:534-537
- pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:554-557
- pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:576-579

Explanation:
Each batch logs at Error level, including the full `ids` slice (up to the batch size, e.g. 32k IDs) and the SQL condition. This is leftover debugging output. It floods the logs and falsely signals errors on a normal cleanup run. It also logs `err` as nil on success. The variables `x, y` are poorly named as well. Remove these logs, or drop them to Debug level without the ID list.

Proposed fix:
~~~go
affected, err := r.deleteByIDs(ctx, "annotation", ids)
return affected, err
~~~

## 2) Severity: HIGH | Type: Bug
Title: Cleanup job interval changed from 10 to 1 minute

Affected:
- pkg/services/cleanup/cleanup.go:77

Explanation:
The ticker was changed to run every minute. This is unrelated to the change and looks like a debugging leftover. It makes every cleanup job (temp files, expired dashboards, and so on) run 10x more often, adding load. Revert it.

Proposed fix:
~~~go
ticker := time.NewTicker(time.Minute * 10)
~~~

## 3) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Title: SQLite parameter-limit workaround is keyed on the configured batch size instead of the ID count, and is fragile

Affected:
- pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:605-618

Explanation:
The limit is 999 only for SQLite older than 3.32; newer versions allow 32766. The code switches to inlined IDs whenever the batch size exceeds 999, so the workaround covers most configurations. The check should be on `len(ids)`, which is what matters. The comment is also inaccurate. Inlining is safe here because the IDs are int64. Still, `fmt.Sprintf` in a loop is O(n²) string concatenation. Use `strings.Builder` or `strings.Join`.

Proposed fix:
~~~go
if r.db.GetDBType() == migrator.SQLite && len(ids) > sqliteParameterLimit {
    parts := make([]string, len(ids))
    for i, v := range ids { parts[i] = strconv.FormatInt(v, 10) }
    sql = fmt.Sprintf(`DELETE FROM %s WHERE id IN (%s)`, table, strings.Join(parts, ","))
}
~~~

## 4) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Title: MaxCount cleanup can loop forever or run wastefully when deletes affect 0 rows

Affected:
- pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:640-654

Explanation:
The loop ends only when a batch affects zero rows. Previously, a single statement did the select and delete together. Now, if IDs are fetched but deletion returns 0 affected rows (for example, rows deleted concurrently by another instance), the loop ends early, which is acceptable. The reverse is worse: fetchIDs is a separate query with a non-transactional read, so a persistently failing delete is returned as an error. Overall the termination logic is acceptable, but the loop's behavior depends on rows-affected semantics, so terminating on `len(ids)==0` would be more robust.

Proposed fix:
~~~go
// terminate on len(ids)==0 rather than affected==0
~~~

## 5) Severity: LOW | Type: Test
Title: Test helper uses require inside the DB session callback and discards the callback's error

Affected:
- pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/cleanup_test.go:273-291

Explanation:
`require.NoError` inside the callback calls FailNow from within the session callback. The callback also returns nil, so errors are never propagated. Return the error instead. Also, the `ID` is set explicitly on the annotations, so a second test case reuses IDs; this relies on the cleanup hook deleting everything first.

Proposed fix:
~~~go
_, err := sess.InsertMulti(...)
if err != nil { return err }
~~~
